name: TigerBeetle
tagline: Purpose-built financial transactions database: double-entry accounts and transfers at very high throughput.
description: TigerBeetle is a distributed database that does one thing: debit/credit accounting. Its schema is fixed to accounts and transfers, with double-entry invariants, balance limits, two-phase (pending) transfers and linked events enforced inside the database. Because the data model is fixed, it can batch thousands of transfers per request and sustain throughput that general-purpose SQL databases struggle with under contention. It is written in Zig with deterministic simulation testing, static memory allocation and Viewstamped Replication across a six-replica cluster. Use it as the ledger next to your general-purpose OLTP database, not as a replacement for it.

pricing.notes: Open source; the company sells enterprise support and managed deployments.

scale.notes: One cluster replicates (not shards) all data across six replicas, which can span zones or regions for fault tolerance.

queryLanguages: TigerBeetle client API (create_accounts, create_transfers, lookups, queries)
strengths: Double-entry invariants, limits and two-phase transfers enforced in the database
Batching gives very high transfer throughput, even on hot accounts
Deterministic simulation testing and strict storage-fault handling
Strictly serializable replication with automatic failover
weaknesses: Fixed schema: accounts and transfers only, with 128-bit user-data fields
Needs a separate OLTP database for everything else
No SQL or ad-hoc query interface
Pre-1.0 versioning with frequent releases to track
useCases: Real-time balance tracking for fintech and brokerages
